faqs.a: A CSS sprite is one image that holds many smaller graphics. Instead of loading ten icon files, the page loads one file and shows each icon by shifting the visible window with the CSS background-position property.

Every separate image file needs its own HTTP request. On slow networks each request adds noticeable delay. One sprite sheet means one request, so icon-heavy pages like navigation bars and toolbars load faster.
faqs.q: Why should I use sprites instead of separate images?

faqs.a: Horizontal works well for a row of toolbar icons, vertical suits menus, and grid is best when you have many icons and want a compact, roughly square sheet. The generated CSS is identical in concept; only the offsets differ.
Without padding, rounding differences in some browsers can reveal a one-pixel sliver of the neighboring image. A few pixels of padding give every sprite a clean border.

Yes, but plan ahead: for retina displays, build the sheet at double size from double-size source images and scale it down with background-size. This generator keeps original dimensions, so prepare your sources accordingly.
faqs.q: Can I use the sprite with responsive or retina designs?

faqs.a: No. The sheet is composed on a canvas element inside your own browser tab. Nothing is sent to any server.

css-sprite-generator.formula:
sheet width (horizontal) = sum of all image widths + padding × (image count + 1)
sheet height (horizontal) = tallest image height + padding × 2

Example offset for image n: x = padding + sum of widths of images before n + padding × (n − 1)
howTo: Click the upload area and select two or more image files (PNG with transparency works best).
Pick a layout: horizontal places images in a row, vertical in a column, grid wraps into columns.
Adjust the padding slider so there is a clean gap between neighboring images.
Type a CSS class prefix (for example icons) that will name all generated classes.
Click Download PNG to save the sprite sheet, then Copy CSS and paste the rules into your stylesheet.

css-sprite-generator.quickAnswer: A sprite generator packs several small images into one larger image (a sprite sheet) and writes the CSS background-position rules for you. This cuts the number of HTTP requests your page makes, which usually means faster loading. Upload your images, choose horizontal, vertical or grid layout, set the padding, then download the PNG sheet and copy the CSS.
css-sprite-generator.workedExample:
You upload three 32 × 32 px icons and choose horizontal layout with 8 px padding.

Sheet width = 32 + 32 + 32 + 8 × (3 + 1) = 96 + 32 = 128 px.
Sheet height = 32 + 8 × 2 = 48 px.

The generated CSS positions are: icon 1 at -8px -8px, icon 2 at -48px -8px, icon 3 at -88px -8px. Each class also carries its own width and height of 32 px, so the browser shows exactly one icon per element.
